ai.description: This gecko reaches 60 mm in snout-vent length. It is brownish-grey with dark, irregular transverse bands and a distinct pale vertebral stripe. It possesses vertically elliptical pupils and lamellae.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Anamalai Hill Gecko is best distinguished by its lack of webbing between the toes and the presence of a distinct, dark, W-shaped marking on the nape of its neck.
ai.habitat: The Anamalai Hill Gecko inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Anamalai Hill Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects on rock surfaces and tree trunks within its humid forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Anamalai Hill Gecko is oviparous, laying a single hard-shelled egg per clutch. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Anamalai Hill Gecko is endemic to the southern Western Ghats, primarily occurring in the high-elevation forests of Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
